reason: Lessee must sue within 6 months of the cause of action, against the statutory 3 years (12 for possession). This cuts the time to enforce rights. 'Notwithstanding Clause 13' carries it into arbitration too (s.43 A&C Act).

Read with the definition in 15A.1: the notice must be given within 30 days of handover, but nothing follows from missing that date. No forfeiture, waiver or discharge, and the refund duty in 3(b), 9(I)(g) and 10(e) stands on its own. It is a contract step only. If you meant late notice to forfeit the deposit, the deed does not say so.

If the claim is not raised within 60 days it is 'deemed to have been waived' and the Lessor 'shall stand discharged'. That extinguishes a right and discharges a party once a set period expires. The deed is from 2006, after the 1997 amendment.

Proceedings must be started within 3 months of the 45-day cure period ends, 'failing which ... precluded from enforcing any remedy'. That is shorter than the statutory 3 years. Binding both parties does not save it. The 'precluded from enforcing any remedy' words are s.28(b) as well.
A 15-day duty to send an interest statement, with no consequence for missing it. The interest right in 3(b) is not extinguished. Same pattern as the plain 'notify within 30 days' look-alike.

Read with 15A.2: 'Restricted Period' is 18 months from expiry or termination and 'Restricted Area' is 2 km. This restrains the Lessee from carrying on its business after the lease ends. The area and time limits do not help (Krishan Murgai, Percept D'Mark). Exception 1 does not apply because no goodwill is sold.
A restriction on how the Lessor lets his own other units, and only during the term and renewals. It does not restrain anyone's trade in the s.27 sense.

3 years from the end of the lease is at least the statutory 3 years for any claim that accrues during the term, so it does not limit time. Edge case: for a claim accruing after the lease ends (an indemnity under GTC-24(a) or 25(c), or a breach of the post-term covenant in GTC-24(h)), it gives less than 3 years from accrual. To that extent it would be void. Please flag this as a possible ambiguity.

Pay first, dispute later. The bill must be paid within the 7-day Protest Window (E.1), but the clause keeps the Lessee's right to dispute and recover ('without prejudice'). No right is extinguished and no time limit is put on suing.

If no written demand is made within 90 days, 'the Lessor shall stand discharged from all liability to refund the Deposit'. That discharges a party once a set period expires. The deed is from 2003, after 1997, so (b) applies.

Read with E.2: the 'Limitation Date' is 3 years from the event giving rise to the claim, which matches the 3 years under Art. 55/113. Caveat: for the indemnities in GTC-24(a) and 25(c), limitation runs from when the loss is actually suffered. If 'event' were read as the underlying act, the clause would cut time and be void to that extent. Read contra proferentem it means accrual, so valid. This is a borderline item.
A user clause that limits what can be done on the Demised Premises only (no voice call centre, no walk-in public). It does not restrain the Lessee's business anywhere else.

Read with E.3 ('Competing Facility' = any non-Lessor premises in Madhapur, Gachibowli or Kondapur): an in-term restraint on carrying on IT/ITES business elsewhere, extended to group companies. The rent is fixed with no turnover share, so the Lessor's legitimate interest is not apparent, and whether it is saved (Gujarat Bottling) cannot be settled from the text. It is very broad and close to void.

For 2 years after surrender the Lessee may not occupy any premises within 5 km for software or ITES business. Drafted as a ban on occupying premises, it is in substance a post-term restraint on carrying on business in the area. No goodwill exception.

The Lessor must sue within 3 months of the sum falling due, against 3 years (Art. 52/55) and 12 years for possession (Art. 67). Note that 3(e) already shuts the Lessor out of the courts for the same claims, which is a separate s.28(a) absolute bar.

Read with 3(g): if the Lessor does not object by the Settlement Date (45 days after intimation), the Lessor is 'deemed ... to have waived all rights to recover'. That extinguishes a right once a set period expires.
A 60-day duty to lodge a written refund claim, with no forfeiture or discharge attached. It is a contract step only.

The clause requires a guarantee under which the Lessee's rights 'shall stand extinguished' unless a claim is made within 6 months. Exception 3 saves such a term only if the period is at least 1 year, so it fails. Void words: 'and all rights of the Lessee thereunder shall stand extinguished, unless ... six (6) months ...'. The duty to furnish the guarantee itself survives. It is unusual for the Lessor to be the one giving the guarantee.
Read with 3(i): notice of an interruption within 15 days of becoming aware of it. No waiver or discharge follows, so the quiet-enjoyment right in 2(d) is not extinguished.
A user clause: office use only, no storage or guest house. It restricts use of the Lessor's premises, not the Lessee's trade elsewhere.

An in-term restraint on setting up another ER-II office within 3 km of the premises, i.e. on business elsewhere, not just on these premises. Following the Session 1 rule this is refer, since the text gives no commercial justification. A question for Session 2: whether a PSU's choice of office location is 'trade or business' at all.
